findings.title: Cleanup ticker silently changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body:
The interval for all background cleanup jobs drops from 10 minutes to 1 minute. This covers temp files, snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, invites, short URLs and query history, not only annotations. The PR description does not mention this, and it looks like a debugging leftover.

`clean()` still uses a 9-minute timeout, which was sized to fit inside the 10-minute interval. With a 1-minute ticker, a slow run is followed almost immediately by the next one, so cleanup can run nearly continuously.

There is no server lock around `clean()`, so every replica in an HA setup now hits the database 10x more often. This adds load and contention on exactly the tables (annotation) where the PR is trying to reduce deadlocks. It should be reverted to 10 minutes.

findings.title: Debug logging left in at Error level, dumping full ID lists every batch
findings.body:
Every batch in CleanAnnotations (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (lines 576, 579) logs via `r.log.Error`. This happens even on the normal path, including the final empty batch where count is 0.

The log lines include the full `ids` slice, which can be up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` entries (tens of thousands in the new test). They also include an `err` field that is always nil at lines 534/554/576.

In production this produces many spurious ERROR entries on every cleanup cycle, multiplied by the new 1-minute ticker. That pollutes logs, can trigger error-based alerting, and can create very large log lines. These should be removed or downgraded to Debug without the ID list.

findings.title: Quadratic string building when inlining IDs for SQLite
findings.body:
`values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` inside the loop allocates and copies the whole accumulated string on every iteration, so the total work is O(n²) in the number of IDs.

This branch only runs when the batch size is above 999, which is exactly the large-batch case. At the batch size of 32767 used in the new test, this amounts to gigabytes of allocation and copying per batch, repeated for every batch until cleanup is done.

Use a `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` into a `[]byte` instead, as `getAccessControlFilter` already does in this file.

findings.title: Bound-parameter DELETE breaks on MySQL/Postgres for very large batch sizes
findings.body:
The old implementation used a subquery with no bind parameters. The new code binds one `?` per ID for every database except SQLite-with-large-batch.

MySQL prepared statements and PostgreSQL both cap a statement at 65535 bind parameters. A user who has configured `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` above that will now get an error on every cleanup run, and annotations will never be cleaned.

The parameter-limit workaround only covers SQLite. Either chunk `ids` into sub-batches below each dialect's limit, or apply the inlining approach (the IDs are trusted int64s read from the DB) for all dialects when the batch is large.

findings.title: Per-subtest cleanup registered after data creation and assertions
findings.body:
`t.Cleanup` that empties `annotation`/`annotation_tag` is registered only after `createTestAnnotations` and two `require`-based count assertions. All subtests share one DB.

If insertion or either count assertion fails, `FailNow` aborts the subtest before the cleanup is registered. The leftover rows then make every later subtest fail its initial count assertion, which hides the original failure.

The cleanup should be registered before inserting the data.
